caption_hook: Massachusetts has been an ice-age sand pile, a lava field and a coast that drifted in from Africa.

layers.name: SANDWICH MORAINE
layers.hook: Cape Cod is a glacier's leftover
layers.what: A great lobe of ice stopped here and piled up sand, gravel and boulders in a long ridge. When it melted, rising seas drowned the lowlands around the ridge, shaping Cape Cod.
layers.bonus: The Cape Cod Canal cuts through this glacial ridge near Sandwich.

layers.name: HOLYOKE BASALT
layers.what: As Pangaea tore apart, lava flooded the Connecticut Valley and cooled into dark basalt. Tilted and eroded, the hard flows now make ridges such as Mount Tom and the Mount Holyoke Range.
layers.bonus: Amherst professor Edward Hitchcock studied the valley's dinosaur tracks and thought giant birds made them.

layers.name: QUINCY GRANITE
layers.what: Hot magma cooled slowly into a blue-gray granite with a speckled grain. Quincy granite was cut from quarries south of Boston and became a major building stone of the 1800s.
layers.bonus: The Granite Railway, built in 1826 near Quincy, hauled stone for the Bunker Hill Monument.

layers.name: STOCKBRIDGE MARBLE
layers.hook: A tropical sea turned to marble
layers.what: Lime mud and shells piled up in a warm sea, then were buried and baked into white marble. Ancient mountain building later pushed it up into the Berkshire valleys.
layers.bonus: Marble from Lee went into the extension of the U.S. Capitol.

layers.name: DEDHAM GRANODIORITE
layers.hook: A rock from the edge of Africa
layers.what: East of Boston, the bedrock belongs to Avalonia, a strip of crust that began near Africa and later fused onto North America. Plymouth Rock is a boulder of this coarse, gray granodiorite.
layers.bonus: Plymouth Rock split in two in 1774 while being moved, and now sits under a portico on the shore.
